author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold a given specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown first name then last name. All specialties render on one page, reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: the directory is served at the address /specialties.html, fixed by the product owner at intake
given the specialties the clinic knows, when the directory is opened, then every one is listed by its stored name
given a specialty two veterinarians hold, when the directory is opened, then both are listed under it by first name and last name
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the directory is opened, then it is listed with no veterinarian under it
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page
given more specialties than one screen holds, when the directory is opened, then all are on the one page and no paging control is offered
given no specialty at all, when the directory is opened, then an empty directory renders rather than failing
given the directory, when it is rendered, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in a stable order
given every page of the system, when each is rendered, then none links to the specialty directory (NG-10)
given the new page, when it is rendered, then it carries the existing navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory (REQ-SYS-001)
given the new page's wording, when the message bundles are checked, then no user-facing text is hard-coded and every key is present in all eleven languages (REQ-LANG-002)
given a specialty name, when the page is rendered in any language, then the name is shown as stored rather than translated
non_goals: a navigation entry or any inbound link to the page (NG-10)
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged by this slice)
paging or filtering the specialty directory
notes: Address fixed by the product owner: GET /specialties.html. Kept out of docs/prd.md prose because that document names no URL; the design owns the route. Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than blocking: which key sets the stable order, and whether an unheld specialty should appear (read narrowly as yes). docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-specialty-directory-entry-point.md; that file is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lives entirely in the existing vet feature package, which already owns Vet and Specialty. It reuses the server-rendered Thymeleaf pattern, the Spring Data repository pattern, and the shared layout fragment. One thing is genuinely new: the page inverts a unidirectional Vet-to-Specialty association, so the specialty-to-veterinarians view must be assembled rather than queried. That assembly is placed in a new immutable read model, SpecialtyDirectory, not in the controller, because architecture-principles.md forbids adding a new business rule to a web controller. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-08-specialty-directory-read-model.md and in system-design.md Contracts.
integration_points: new route GET /specialties.html on a new SpecialtyController in the vet package; VetController keeps /vets.html and /vets unchanged
new SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty,Integer> exposing a read-only findAll(); mirrors VetRepository's minimal Spring Data surface rather than PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository surface
SpecialtyDirectory.of(Collection<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>) is a pure static factory; the controller calls it and puts the result in the model, holding no rule itself
the template renders through fragments/layout with a menu key matching no navigation item, so the standard navigation renders (REQ-SYS-001) and no new entry appears (NG-10)
Vet.specialties is EAGER and VetRepository.findAll() is @Transactional(readOnly=true), so the grouped model is fully materialized before rendering under spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

patterns.description: the .html route plus model attribute plus view-name shape the new controller copies; grep-confirmed (no IDE oracle connected in this dispatch)
full name rendered in the template as ${...firstName + ' ' + lastName}; the directory renders holders the same way, keeping the display format in the view
Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName) sorting in Java rather than SQL; the directory's ordering follows this precedent
@WebMvcTest plus MockMvc plus @MockitoBean repository; SpecialtyControllerTests mirrors it with both repositories stubbed

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 is the largest hidden cost. I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings flags any template line with literal text between tags unless that same line contains #{, a th:text/th:utext attribute, or is bracket-only. A heading split across two lines from its text trips it.
risks.mitigation: The page needs ZERO new message keys. Reuse the existing keys the vet list already uses: #{specialties} for the heading, #{name} for the specialty column, #{vets} for the holders column, #{none} for a specialty with no holder. Keep every visible-text tag and its th:text on one line. If a new key is truly wanted, add it to messages.properties AND the nine translated bundles (_de,_es,_fa,_hi,_ja,_ko,_pt,_ru,_tr). Do NOT add it to messages_en.properties: that file is deliberately empty (fallback) and the sync test skips it. Eleven bundles exist; nine are enforced against the base.

risks.risk: Specialty and veterinarian names are stored data rendered into HTML.
risks.mitigation: Render with th:text only. Thymeleaf's default escaping stays on; no th:utext anywhere on the page. The PRD requires names shown as stored, so no message lookup wraps them.

risks.risk: Ordering by name in SQL would follow each vendor's collation, the same divergence class as the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect already recorded in system-design.md Known Defects.
risks.mitigation: Order in Java inside the read model: specialties by name, then holders by last name then first name. One comparator, one order on all three vendors, testable with no database.

risks.risk: Every seeded specialty is held by at least one veterinarian (h2/data.sql rows 8-16), so no integration test against seed data can observe the unheld-specialty case.
risks.mitigation: Cover it in SpecialtyDirectoryTests as a plain unit test and in SpecialtyControllerTests with stubbed repositories.

risks.risk: A read model holding Vet entity references would not be immutable or equal by value, and the persistence-entity exception in architecture-principles.md explicitly does not cover value objects.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory carries copied String name values, not entity references, with defensive copies of its lists. Suggested shape: one package-private top-level record SpecialtyDirectory with nested records for a per-specialty row and a holder's first/last name.

risks.risk: Caching SpecialtyRepository would widen Open Question 5 (vet cache has no eviction configured).
risks.mitigation: Leave SpecialtyRepository uncached. Recorded in the ADR and in system-design.md Contracts.

risks.risk: NG-10 requires no inbound link, and the test theNavigationShouldNotLinkToTheSpecialtyDirectory must actually be able to fail.
risks.mitigation: Write it as a resource-scanning test over src/main/resources/templates asserting no href or th:href resolves to /specialties.html, in the style of I18nPropertiesSyncTest. Scanning only fragments/layout.html would pass vacuously.

notes: Two PRD open questions resolved as design guidance. (1) A specialty no veterinarian holds appears with an empty holder list; grouping is driven by the specialty collection, so this falls out of the design rather than needing a branch. (2) Stable order is: specialties ascending by name, then holders ascending by last name then first name, both fixed in Java. Vocabulary: docs/ubiquitous-language.md canonicalizes 'Specialty directory' and lists 'Specialty list' under Avoid, so the template is specialtyDirectory.html and no symbol is named SpecialtyList. 'Vet' stays the code short form. Placement: a separate SpecialtyController rather than a third route on VetController, per the naming rule that a controller is prefixed by the domain noun or surface it serves. GraalVM needs no new runtime hint; PetClinicRuntimeHints registers messages/* and the template sits under the already-supported templates root. No new dependency. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, nothing to judge. Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-08-specialty-directory-read-model.md (new), docs/adr/README.md (index row), docs/system-design.md (Package Structure vet line, Contracts read-model paragraph and three rows, provenance banner sentence covering post-survey additions). The three new Contracts rows are marked as designed but not yet in the working tree.

author: feature-implementer
notes: Self-review walked the nine clauses. Two deliberate choices a reviewer should weigh. (1) Grouping key is the specialty id, not the name, so two rows sharing a name stay distinct; SpecialtyDirectory.of therefore refuses a specialty with no id, naming it in the message, rather than collapsing every unsaved specialty onto a null key. (2) The unheld-specialty case is asserted on the model the page was given rather than re-derived, since seed data holds every specialty. NG-10 is guarded by scanning every template under src/main/resources/templates for the literal specialties.html, which catches a menuItem link parameter as well as an href. IDE static-analysis pre-check: not run, IDE not consulted. No configuration change, no new dependency, no runtime hint, no message-bundle change.
summary: GET /specialties.html renders the specialty directory: every stored specialty by name with the veterinarians holding it, first name then last. The inverse of the unidirectional Vet-to-Specialty association is assembled in memory by the new SpecialtyDirectory read model (immutable record carrying copied name values, ordering fixed in Java: specialties by name, holders by last then first name). SpecialtyController binds the route, calls the factory, selects the view; it holds no rule. SpecialtyRepository exposes a read-only, uncached findAll(). The template vets/specialtyDirectory.html renders through fragments/layout with a menu key matching no navigation item, so the standard navigation shows and no new entry appears (NG-10). Zero new message keys: the page reuses specialties, name, vets, none. 14 new tests, all green; full suite green.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyDirectory.html renders every data-derived value through th:text (entry.name, holder.firstName + ' ' + holder.lastName) with Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping on. No th:utext, no th:inline, no expression preprocessing, no request-derived value in an href or attribute. Class sweep across src/main/resources/templates/vets/ found no unsafe construct.

Exposed surface: the one new endpoint is GET /specialties.html, read-only, no request parameters, no path variables, no binder. It re-projects exactly the data /vets.html already publishes unauthenticated (veterinarian first and last name, specialty name) with no new field or data class. Against system-design.md's Security Context baseline (demonstration app, no authn/authz by design) the change adds no new exposure category and leaves the application no weaker; NG-10's no-navigation-entry decision is a product choice, correctly not relied on as a control. Judged acceptable.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository is a Spring Data derived findAll() with no query text; no string concatenation reaches a query. Read path is @Transactional(readOnly = true). No mass-assignment surface (no @ModelAttribute, no request-bound type, no identifier binding).

Error disclosure: the IllegalArgumentException from SpecialtyDirectory.entryFor carries a stored specialty name, which is clinical taxonomy data, not a credential, connection string, session identifier, or PII, so it does not violate the secret-disclosure row of security-principles.md. server.error.include-message is unset, so Boot's default 'never' leaves error.html's ${message} empty; even were it enabled, the disclosed value is already public on this very page. The branch is additionally unreachable from findAll(), which returns persisted rows only.

Unbounded findAll() with no pagination or cache: the exposure is availability only, matching the pre-existing unbounded, uncached read pattern elsewhere in the app, and specialty cardinality is bounded by clinic taxonomy rather than by any request. No new attacker-controlled amplification (the response size is independent of the request). Not a security finding under the project's threat model.
Supply chain: no build.gradle, settings.gradle, or dependency change in the change set, and no new runtime hint or configuration property. Nothing to verify against NVD for this pass.
Secrets: full change-set scan for credential-shaped literals returned nothing; no configuration or properties file is touched.

A caller reading only the method's contract has no signal that an unsaved specialty aborts the whole call; the class-level Javadoc mentions the general read-model shape but not this specific failure mode either.
findings.fix: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag to the `of(...)` Javadoc describing that a specialty without a stored id fails the whole call.

checkFormat and compileJava/compileTestJava pass clean

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test body itself contains a Files.walk().filter().forEach() with a nested for-loop and an if-statement scanning template lines. testing-principles.md's Agent Decision Checklist item 4 ('Linearity: No branching or loops in the test body') and the Assertions section ('No branching in assertions... Use collection-aware assertions instead') both forbid this. The scan is legitimate (it is what makes the test able to fail — confirmed: it reads templates from disk and is not vacuous), but the iteration belongs in a helper, not inline in the test method.
findings.fix: Extract the Files.walk/filter/forEach/for-loop into a private static method, e.g. `referencesToSpecialtyDirectory()` returning List<String>, so the test body reduces to `List<String> references = referencesToSpecialtyDirectory(); assertThat(references).isEmpty();` — straight-line, matching the pattern already used by readLines().

findings.description: The private helpers `specialty(int id, String name)` and `vet(String firstName, String lastName, Specialty... specialties)` are byte-for-byte duplicated across the two test classes. testing-principles.md's Testing Vocabulary section calls for shared vocabulary extraction ('Extract shared test utilities into a common base class or utility module') and Agent Decision Checklist item 14 ('Zero duplication: Reusable patterns in the shared vocabulary?').
findings.fix: Move the two factory methods into a shared test-support class in the vet test package (e.g. VetFixtures) and have both test classes call it, instead of maintaining two copies.

approved_aspects: All 8 PRD-named tests (prd-entry line 2 test_names) are present; the 2 additional tests are justified — theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryTheStandardNavigation covers the explicit REQ-SYS-001 acceptance criterion and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRefuseASpecialtyThatWasNeverStored covers a real defensive branch in SpecialtyDirectory.of

The unheld-specialty case is genuinely exercised: seed data (db/h2/data.sql rows 8-16) holds every specialty, so both SpecialtyDirectoryTests (pure unit, no seed data at all) and SpecialtyControllerTests (stubbed repositories via @MockitoBean) construct the case directly rather than relying on unreachable seed state — verified by reading data.sql

theNavigationShouldNotLinkToTheSpecialtyDirectory is not vacuous: it walks every .html under src/main/resources/templates from disk and would fail if any template linked to specialties.html; confirmed non-self-referential against the new template
